evidence: Compared 'I'd leave out forgiving them and picturing their childhood here.' with the source 'I'd leave out forgiving them and picturing their childhood.': identical except for the final 'here'. It does what the_change says. In the paragraph 'here' is anchored by 'this is a gentler cousin' two sentences up (this exercise) and by 'Whoever hurt you might come to mind, too' (the moment the advice is about), so it reads as 'in this exercise' and not as a place or the whole guide. The source sentence, read alone, could pass for a standing stance against forgiving or understanding whoever hurt you; 'here' keeps the same instruction and states the scope the paragraph already implies, so the meaning is kept. The word adds the mild implication that those things may be fine elsewhere; that is the narrowing the change asks for, and nothing in this section contradicts it (I saw only this section, so I could not check the rest of the guide). It is a scope word, not a rarer-word swap (T15 absent) and not a restatement or a tacked-on completion (T29, T11 absent); the sentence still adds a new instruction at the end of the paragraph and 'I'd' is the source's own (T01 absent, C03 absent). C02: 'them' and 'their' are 'Whoever hurt you' and still read correctly. Went through T01-T29 and C01-C04: the paragraph's compressed reassurance cadence ('normal breathing is fine', 'might come to mind, too') is the source's own and one word does not add to it, so T02 and T22 are not made worse by the edit. Linter D9 'follows the source order': a one-word addition cannot do otherwise and preservation requires it; T13 and T09 are not at issue for a single added word; accepted as answered by the context.
